prompt: Build a complete persistent task HTTP API in one source file. The first command-line argument is the TCP port. Run until terminated. The working directory initially contains an empty public/ directory and no data files. Store data outside public/, using relative paths. Requests are sequential; concurrency is out of scope. Contract: GET /health -> 200 {"status":"ok"}. GET /tasks -> 200 JSON array of tasks ordered by increasing ID, initially []. A task has exactly {"id": integer, "title": string, "done": boolean}. POST /tasks accepts {"title": string}, requires a nonempty title, allocates sequential positive IDs starting at 1, sets done=false, and returns 201 with the task. GET /tasks/{id} returns 200 with the task. PUT /tasks/{id} accepts {"title": string, "done": boolean}; a nonempty title is required, done defaults to false if omitted; replace those fields and return 200 with the updated task. DELETE /tasks/{id} removes it and returns 200 {"deleted":true}. Missing IDs return 404; noninteger or nonpositive IDs return 400. Malformed JSON, missing/empty titles and wrong field types return 400, without mutating data or consuming IDs. All error responses are JSON objects with a nonempty error string. Every response has application/json content type. Persist tasks and the next ID before acknowledging a successful mutation; return 500 JSON error on storage failures. Restarting the process in the same directory must preserve creates, updates, deletions and the ID counter: never reuse deleted IDs. Support arbitrary titles including quotes and Unicode with proper JSON escaping. Handle fallible operations. Return only source code.
